::: {.callout-note title="Updated June 2026"}
The original version of this post embedded an interactive [D3](https://d3js.org/) flight map hosted on bl.ocks.org. That service has since shut down, taking the visualization with it. I've replaced it below with a static map rebuilt from the same flight data — every flight through August 2014. There's a [companion post](../2026-06-20-flight-map-redrawn/) with the map extended to the present.
:::

As of this week, I am officially no longer an astrophysicist. I start my next career as a data scientist in about a month. It's been a fantastic experience for me both personally and professionally. Michael Murphy was an incredibly patient and encouraging boss from whom I learned more than I hoped.

Coming into this job I hoped to learn a ton, and I have, but many opportunities and experiences were completely unexpected. From observing at observatories like ESO's VLT in Chile and Keck in Hawaii, to being in an IMAX film. Finally, the amazing amount of travel that my position granted me was life altering.

This is not my big farewell post, as I still have a week and a bit in Australia, but I had trouble sleeping last night so I decided to make a fun [D3](https://d3js.org/) map of all of the flights that I've taken during my time as a postdoc -- starting with the flights from DFW (Dallas-Forth Worth) to LAX (Los Angeles) to MEL (Melbourne) in August 2011!

::: {.column-page}
![Every flight I'd taken during the postdoc, through August 2014.](/assets/images/flights/flights-map-2014.svg)
:::

Ok future, let's see where we go from here.
